newsitem.title: FRANCE: French businessman buys UAP properties.
newsitem.headline: French businessman buys UAP properties.

text.p: A French financier has bought 12 downtown Paris buildings owned by Union des Assurances de Paris (UAP) for 335 million francs in what may be a futher sign that the capital city's long-running property slump is ending.

A spokesman for the insurer which is merging with another French insurance company Axa said on Friday that Walter Butler, who runs his own investment group, Walter Capital Partners, bought a portfolio made up of nine apartment buildings and three office sites.

While the size of the purchase was relatively small, it is the first time a local investor has entered the market until now dominated by so-called U.S. "vulture funds" specialising in distressed property assets.
"We share the view of non-domestic investors that the French market is going to emerge from the crisis," Butler said in an interview.
"There is an interesting opportunity given the state of the market and interest rates," he added.
He believes a combination of low prices and low interest rates could help the Paris market pick up in much the same way that New York and London have seen their real estate markets recover.
The transaction was carried out at an average price of 17,500 francs per square metre, less than half of what they might have fetched just five years ago.
The purchase represents Walter Butler's first foray into real estate and he did not rule out the possibility that it could be an area of development for his group.
He recently tried without success to buy France's loss-making, state-owned Societe Francaise de Production (SFP) film studios.
For UAP, the operation was marginal because the company has 3.5 million square metres of housing and office space.
UAP late last year announced it was merging with Axa to form Axa-UAP which will be the world's second largest insurer.
